summary: Two MAJ findings block approval: §10 lists 10 'open questions' but 7 of them are explicitly resolved at plan-doc level or self-declared non-questions, making the section structurally misleading and failing DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (xi); and the plan-doc architecture (§5) does not name when or how cross-repo governance notifications to CT / ACC / mapp-estate-regression are sent during the cascade, leaving a coordination gap that implementation slices will have no plan-doc anchor for.

findings.title: §10 presents 7 of 10 'open questions' that are explicitly resolved at plan-doc level or self-declared non-questions — the section fails its stated purpose
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md lines 224–235. Q1 closes with 'Resolved at plan-doc level: stick to the D-035 enumeration'; Q2 closes with 'Resolved at plan-doc level: invariant 4'; Q3 closes with 'Resolved at plan-doc level: invariant 5'; Q5 closes with 'Resolved at plan-doc level: no overlays in v1'; Q6 closes with 'Resolved at plan-doc level: deferred to D-046 at 024G'; Q8 closes with 'Resolved at plan-doc level: adopter-side review shape is per the adopter's repo policy'; Q10 explicitly states 'Not an open question — surfaced for transparency.' Only Q4, Q7, and Q9 are genuinely open. DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (xi) requires §10 to 'capture questions that should be revisited at each implementation slice (10 questions)'; the review-completeness-package.json instruction explicitly flags: 'An open question that has a paragraph of Resolved at plan-doc level: X is NOT actually open — that's a closed decision masquerading as a question.'
findings.recommendation: Remove Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q8 from §10 — their resolutions are already embodied in the plan-doc body (invariants, §5.1, §9) and repeating them as 'open questions' misleads implementation-slice authors about what requires re-evaluation. Remove Q10 which self-declares it is not an open question. Renumber the remaining genuinely-open entries (Q4 → Q1, Q7 → Q2, Q9 → Q3). If additional open questions exist that are appropriate to surface, add them to reach a meaningful count; if only 3 genuine open items remain, §10 should contain exactly 3 entries. The section header should reflect the actual count.

findings.title: Plan-doc §5 architecture does not name cross-repo coordination points: when and how governance notifications go to CT / ACC / mapp-estate-regression during cascade
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md §5.1–§5.5 (lines 90–159) and §6 (lines 162–173). The per-adopter onboarding contract (§5.2) defines the adopter PR, SCP-side cascade slice PR, invocation log, and post-bake observation entry — but names no cross-repo notification step. The DISPATCH-NOTE scope table (line 31) correctly marks cross-repo notification as OUT for 024A since 'cross-repo coordination starts when cascade rollout begins (024C onwards)' — but the plan-doc body never names what that coordination looks like or when it fires. The reference_ct_notifications.md memory entry identifies ~/Projects/control-tower/governance/docs/notifications/ as the cross-repo conversation log; TF-023A-002 (STATUS.md line 202) carries forward the v1.2.0 release notification that was deferred from 023D to 023E 'until adopters can opt in' — WP-SCP-024 does not reference this TF or establish its own notification pattern. Implementation slices 024C–024F will have no plan-doc anchor for when to file CT/ACC/mapp-estate-regression notifications.
findings.recommendation: Add a §5.6 (or subsection of §5.2) titled 'Cross-repo coordination' that names: (a) at 024C kickoff, a notification is filed to the CT governance notifications path (~/Projects/control-tower/governance/docs/notifications/) announcing the estate cascade start and naming the 5-cohort, the canary-first ordering, and the observation-window SLO; (b) TF-023A-002 (cross-repo v1.2.0 notification) is incorporated into the 024C kickoff notification or resolved as a separate step at 024C; (c) ACC is notified at 024C because ACC's MCP dispatcher consults SCP at plan-decompose, and estate-wide branch-protection changes affecting the cascade cohort are material to ACC's operating context; (d) mapp-estate-regression is notified when mapp-doc-agent and recommender cascade (024E) since those repos fall within mapp-estate-regression's tracking scope. Each cascade slice DISPATCH-NOTE then references this §5.6 for its coordination step.

findings.title: §10 Q10 ('Cascade slice CI cost') is self-declared non-open but included in the 10-question count — creates a numbering distortion beyond CMP-MAJ-001
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md line 235: '10. Cascade slice CI cost — each cascade slice's PR adds invocation-log + DISPATCH-NOTE + reviews JSON. The SCP-side CI burden is small (mostly docs). Not an open question — surfaced for transparency.' The DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (xi) requires 10 open questions; including a self-declared non-question to reach 10 artificially inflates the count. This compounds CMP-MAJ-001 but is separately actionable regardless of how Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5/Q6/Q8 are resolved.
findings.recommendation: Either remove Q10 entirely (it contains no information that could affect an implementation slice decision) or, if the cost transparency is material, fold it into the §7 risk surface as a named R-024-NN row documenting the accepted CI-cost posture. Do not include self-declared non-questions in §10.

findings.title: §8 Threshold A optional criterion uses 'Optional, D-046 to confirm' framing without naming what happens if D-046 drops the optional surface — leaves Threshold A measurability indeterminate on that row
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md lines 206–207: '(Optional, D-046 to confirm) `scp.consult_estate_status` MCP method live OR existing `scp.consult_scorecard` extended to surface cascade status.' The review-completeness-package.json instruction requires the Threshold A criterion to be 'measurable + testable.' An optional criterion that either a new method OR an extension of an existing method may or may not exist is not measurable at plan-doc time — there is no binary pass/fail test for it. The 'D-046 to confirm' parenthetical defers the measurability determination to a future decision, leaving the criterion unverifiable until 024G.
findings.recommendation: Reframe this row as a forward-looking note rather than a Threshold A criterion: 'D-046 will decide whether `scp.consult_estate_status` ships as a new MCP method or is rolled into existing `scp.consult_scorecard`; this criterion is informational at plan-doc time and not part of the binary Threshold A pass/fail gate.' Alternatively, split the row: the binary Threshold A pass/fail gate is the 4 mandatory criteria above it; the optional MCP decision is a D-046 topic recorded in §9, not in §8.

findings.title: §5.2 per-adopter onboarding contract step (3) sequences 'enable-required-check.sh invocation' AFTER 'both PRs merge' — creates a subtle ordering ambiguity vs. §5.4 which names a pre-condition check ('has not run successfully at least once on a recent PR') that implies the wrapper must merge and green-CI before the script runs
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md §5.2 item 3 (line 116): 'enable-required-check.sh invocation — operator-run from local machine after both PRs merge + post-bake clean.' §5.4 (line 145): 'A safety check: refuses to invoke against a target repo whose policy-check / scp/policy-check check has not run successfully at least once on a recent PR (proving the wrapper PR landed + the federation primitive is functional in that adopter's environment).' The phrase 'after both PRs merge + post-bake clean' in §5.2 item 3 implies the invocation happens at the END of the post-bake observation window, not immediately after the adopter wrapper PR merges. But §5.4's safety-check language implies the script is run before the post-bake window starts (to enable the required check so that post-bake observation can begin). The actual intended sequence is: wrapper PR merges → green-CI run observed → invocation-log entry committed → script invoked → required check enabled → post-bake window begins. §5.2 item 3 should clarify this ordering.
findings.recommendation: Amend §5.2 item (3) to read: 'enable-required-check.sh invocation — operator-run from local machine after the adopter wrapper PR merges + at least one green policy-check CI run is observed on the adopter repo (satisfying the §5.4 safety check), and BEFORE the post-bake observation window begins.' Append to §5.2: 'Steps (3) and (4) are not concurrent — (3) enables the gate that (4) observes.'

findings.title: §6 slice table 024D row missing D-NNN filing — asymmetric with 024C (D-045) and 024G (D-046), and no explicit note that 024D intentionally files no decision
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md §6 table (lines 163–172). 024C acceptance criteria: 'D-045 filed.' 024G acceptance criteria: 'D-046 filed.' 024D acceptance criteria: 'control-tower `policy-check / scp/policy-check` required-check live; ≥1 Renovate-bump-propagation cycle merged clean' — no D-NNN reference and no note that this is intentional. 024E and 024F similarly have no D-NNN filing. §9 explains why D-044/D-045/D-046 land at their specific slices; the absence of a decision at 024D is intentional (D-045 at 024C already ratifies the per-adopter onboarding contract pattern that 024D reuses). But a reader scanning §6 for slice completeness may question whether 024D is missing something.
findings.recommendation: Add a footnote or inline note to the 024D, 024E, and 024F rows: 'No new D-NNN filed — D-045 (at 024C) ratifies the per-adopter onboarding contract pattern that this slice inherits.' One sentence per row is sufficient.
